q: Who can apply?
a: Business Cup 2.0 is open to Bachelor’s and Master’s students.

q: Do I need to be a developer?
a:
No.

You don’t need to come from a specific background or have a specific role. Different skills can contribute to building a strong product.

q: Do I need a team to apply?
a:
No.

You can apply:

• with an existing team
• solo
• looking for a team

q: How big can my team be?
a:
Teams can have 1–3 people.

You can participate solo, as a pair or as a team of three.

q: Can my teammates be from different universities?
a:
Yes.

Cross-university teams are welcome.

q: What if I don’t have a team?
a:
Apply anyway.

If you’re selected and looking for teammates, we’ll help with team matching before the hackathon.

q: Can I participate solo?
a:
Yes.

You can build on your own or request team matching.

q: When do applications close?
a:
Applications close on November 9, 2026.

Spots are limited, so we recommend applying early.

q: How do I apply?
a:
Complete the application form and tell us how you want to participate:

• with an existing team
• solo
• looking for a team

q: What happens after I apply?
a:
We’ll review your application and let you know if you’ve been selected for Business Cup 2.0.

Selected participants will receive an official invitation with the next steps.

q: How does selection work?
a:
Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis.

You don’t need to wait until the application deadline to hear from us.

q: When will I know if I’m in?
a: Invitations are sent on a rolling basis as applications are reviewed.

q: How many teams will participate?
a: Up to 100 teams will be invited to Business Cup 2.0.

q: If I already have a team, does everyone need to apply?
a:
Yes.

Registration is individual, so every team member needs to submit an application and indicate their team status in the form.

q: When and where is Business Cup 2.0?
a:
November 14–15, 2026

Nazarbayev University
Astana, Kazakhstan

q: Is Business Cup 2.0 online or offline?
a:
Fully offline.

You’ll need to be at Nazarbayev University in Astana for the hackathon.

q: How long is the hackathon?
a:
Business Cup 2.0 takes place over one weekend.

The actual build window is 24 hours — from the moment the case drops on Saturday until submissions close on Sunday.

q: What does Saturday look like?
a:
NOVEMBER 14

10:00 — Check-in & Welcome Pack Pickup
11:00–12:00 — Opening & Case Briefing
12:00 — CASE DROP

Your 24 hours start here.

q: What does Sunday look like?
a:
NOVEMBER 15

12:00 — SUBMISSION DEADLINE
12:00–15:00 — Jury Review & Top 10 Selection
15:00–15:30 — Finalists Announcement
15:30–16:30 — Finalists Check-in & Pitch Prep
16:30–18:00 — TOP 10 LIVE PITCHES
18:00–18:30 — Jury Deliberation
18:30–19:00 — Awards Ceremony & Closing

Each finalist gets:
5 min pitch + 2 min Q&A

₸5,000,000 is on the line.

q: Do we actually have 24 hours to build?
a:
Yes.

The case drops at 12:00 on November 14, and submissions close at 12:00 on November 15.

How your team organizes those 24 hours is up to you.

q: Do I need to prepare anything before the hackathon?
a:
You won’t receive the case in advance.

Come ready to build.

q: What exactly will we build?
a:
Nice try.

The case drops on November 14.

What we can tell you now: you’ll need to turn the challenge into a working digital product within 24 hours.

q: Will we know the case in advance?
a:
No.

Everyone gets the case at the hackathon.

The clock starts from there.

q: Do we need to build a working product?
a:
Yes.

Business Cup 2.0 goes beyond ideas and slides. By the submission deadline, your team needs to have a working digital product.

q: Is this a case competition or a hackathon?
a:
Business Cup 2.0 brings both together.

You get a case to solve — but instead of stopping at analysis and a presentation, you have 24 hours to turn your solution into a product.

q: What do we need to submit?
a:
A working digital product and the materials required for the final evaluation.

Detailed submission requirements will be shared with participants before the hackathon.

q: How does the final work?
a:
After submissions close, the jury reviews the products and selects the Top 10 teams.

Those teams advance to the live final.

q: How much time do finalists get?
a:
Each finalist gets:

5 minutes to pitch

2 minutes for jury Q&A

q: Who will be on the jury?
a:
The jury will include Zimran leaders and product operators.

The final lineup will be announced separately.

q: How will the products be judged?
a:
The jury will evaluate both the working product and the final pitch.

Detailed judging criteria will be shared with participants before the hackathon.

q: What is the prize pool?
a:
₸5,000,000

The total prize pool for Business Cup 2.0 is ₸5 million.

q: How many teams will win?
a: There will be 1st, 2nd and 3rd place winners.

q: How will the ₸5,000,000 be split?
a: The final prize distribution will be announced separately.

q: Is Business Cup 2.0 a hiring program?
a:
No.

Business Cup 2.0 is a hackathon, not a hiring process.

q: Can Business Cup lead to opportunities at Zimran?
a:
Yes.

Strong participants may be considered for relevant future opportunities at Zimran.

Participation itself does not guarantee employment.

q: What happens after Business Cup?
a:
For most participants, Business Cup ends after the final on November 15.

For standout participants, the conversation with Zimran may continue beyond the hackathon.

q: I still have a question. Who can I contact?
a: tech@zimran.io
